observations: Identity: the runtime did not give me a task or agent identity, so task is null. The parent must record the actual Agent ID returned by its Agent tool, and must not invent one.

What I read, in order: docs/REVISION-AND-REVIEWS.md, docs/PROMPTS.md, cli/stage-review.mjs (prepare instructions, lines 100-179), and this request JSON, which includes the script and the recorded first reading. Then I opened these PNGs with Read: workflow/storyboards-unnumbered/page-02.png, workflow/storyboards/page-02.png (numbered), workflow/review/page-01.png and page-02.png (composed art with lettering), and workflow/reading-flow/page-02.json. I also read source/original.txt and source/REVISION-2026-11-11.md. Because this is a comparison review, I read the script before the images.

Limit on what I checked: the request hashes the numbered storyboard as an SVG. I viewed storyboards/page-02.png. Its layout and text match the unnumbered PNG, but I did not confirm that it was exported from the current SVG.

Unnumbered PNG: 4 panels (wide top, two middle, wide bottom). Natural order: P1 caption at top-left, then the teal label at top-right. P2 Ananya's balloon. P3 Meera's balloon, then the WELBUK CARE label at the bottom. P4 'One team. Better coordination.' This matches the script order 02-1[1,2], 02-2[1], 02-3[1,2], 02-4[1].

First-reader issue (1), the P4 speaker could be Meera: the art resolves it. In review/page-02.png Ananya's face is at about x305-400. The balloon starts at about x425 and does not cover her face. The short tail goes to her open, smiling mouth, while Meera at the right has a closed smile. The placeholder name label being clipped matters only in the guide image.

First-reader issue (2), the P1 caption and label sit flush on the frame corners: in the art these read as deliberate corner inset boxes, and both are fully legible. This is a lettering-stage cosmetic, not a storyboard problem.

First-reader issue (3), Welbuk is not explained: acceptable. The source gives exactly this caption, and the labels 'WELBUK PRACTICE for the clinic' and 'WELBUK CARE for clinic staff' state the product roles. Issue (4), the label order: agreed, it is clear.

Script against source: all four lines and the caption are verbatim from source PAGE 2. In 02-2 the tail lands at Ananya's temple or hair, inside her face box [365,655,105,115], and nothing else competes for it. In 02-3 the balloon tail goes to Meera's face [851,739,51,66], and her phone hand (protected box) is not covered.

The unnumbered page reads left to right and top to bottom without hesitation. The only multi-item panels are 02-1 (caption at top-left, then label at top-right in the same band) and 02-3 (balloon at top, label at bottom). Neither creates a proximity trap.
The automatic reading-flow warning on 02-1 (step 1 to step 2 shares a vertical band) is a normal left-to-right move along one row, not a backtrack.
In 02-4 the balloon sits between the two figures. Ananya's open mouth and the tail direction settle the speaker, and Meera's silent smile reads as the nod reply.

transitions.observation: Page 1 ends in the morning reception, with Ananya resolving to 'make the rest simpler'. Page 2 opens with a sunset window, an office desk and a laptop setup form, under the caption 'The clinic begins its Welbuk onboarding.' The change of time and place is carried by the light and the caption, and the cause (her resolve) leads into the effect (onboarding).
Same office, same sunset window. Ananya goes from typing (over-the-shoulder) to finger-at-chin with her right hand on the trackpad. The before/after records match what is drawn.
Same evening office: window blind, laptop on the desk, an empty chair. Meera has joined, holding the staff phone with a calendar icon, and 'And our team...' continues Ananya's line.

A two-shot in the same office. Ananya is seated at left, Meera stands at right holding the phone at her side, and the laptop is turned toward the reader. Phone and laptop continuity is consistent with 02-3.

From the evening office to bright daylight at the reception desk. The caption 'A later morning:' anchors the jump. Meera appears in the same blue kurta and braid, and the desk now has a monitor instead of the paper registers from 01-2, which gives a visible before and after.

readingReview.comparison: Agreements: the first reader's natural order matches the script order exactly. Concern (1), P4 speaker ambiguity: resolved by the accepted art, as described above (face uncovered, open mouth, tail toward Ananya). Concern (2), corner boxes: a lettering cosmetic only, legible in the art. Concern (3), no time marker: the sunset light and the onboarding caption are enough. The meaning of Welbuk is carried by the product labels, as the source intends. Concern (4): agreed. No skips and no unresolved ambiguity.
